name.evidence: Red case label, PDF image 1: 'CASE NO. 12 / NORTHERN DISTRICT / EL PRIMER CANON or RIO DE LOS BERRENDOS GRANT / J.F. DYE CLAIMANT'. Transcript title, stamped PAGE NO. 1 (image 3): '"El Primer Canon" or "Rio de los Berrendos", J.F. Dye Claimant'.

year.evidence: Spanish titulo (Documento No. 1), stamped PAGE NO. 18 (image 21): 'Dado en Monterey Mayo veinte y dos, de mil ocho cientos cuarenta y cuatro. Man.l Micheltorena'. The District Court papers in the same file caption him 'Job F. Dye', not John: clerk's endorsement 'The United States v. Job. F. land_case.evidence: Red label image 1 'CASE NO. 12 / NORTHERN DISTRICT'; flyleaf image 2 'LAND CASE 12 ND pgs. 101'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_nd012.pdf. outcome.evidence: Commission: 'Decree of Final Confirmation' delivered 18 Dec 1853, stamped PAGE NO. 6-7 (images 9-10), text at stamped PAGE NO. 9 (image 12) 'It is ordered that the said Claim be confirmed to the extent and quantity of Six Square Leagues'. District Court on the United States' appeal AFFIRMED: 'the said decree and decision of the said Commission be and the same is hereby in all things affirmed ... that the claim of the appellee the said Francisco Dye be confirmed to the extent and quantity of six square leagues' (stamped PAGE NO. 94-95, images 93-94), Final Decree filed April 5, 1861 (stamped PAGE NO. 89, image 88). Register 'Confirmed' verified at both levels.

corrections.grantee: Grant decree gives only 'D. Francisco Dye' (stamped p.17, image 20) / 'Don Francisco Dye' in the sworn translation (stamped p.20, image 23). The District Court record in this same file names him JOB F. Dye three times (stamped pp. 89, 98, 100 = images 88, 97, 99), never John. Register's 'John Francisco Dye' should read 'Job Francisco (Job Francis) Dye'.

notes: Same man throughout: claimant = grantee, so no claimant/grantee substitution here. CAUTION on the day of the grant: three different days circulate inside this one file, all 1844 - the titulo and the expediente decree both say 22 May 1844 (stamped pp. 18, 27-28), the Commission's opinion says 'the 20th of May 1844' (stamped PAGE NO. 7, image 10), and the District Court opinion says 'dated 30. May 1844' (stamped PAGE NO. 90, image 89). The grant instrument governs: 22 May 1844. The register only carries the year, so this does not change the year grade. NOTE ON THE 'John' READING: the Bancroft's own digicoll record title also says 'John Francisco Dye, Claimant', so the register may simply have inherited the catalog's expansion of 'J.F.'; the manuscript itself says Job. Also in file: 1861 District Court order annulling the returned survey and directing a new one (stamped pp. 100-101, images 99-100), so the 1871 patent date in the register is plausible but is NOT in this file. ACCESS NOTE: digicoll.lib.berkeley.edu is behind an AWS WAF JS challenge as of 2026-09-09 16:35 UTC - curl and urllib get HTTP 202 + a goku challenge page for both /record/ and /files/ URLs, so fetch_case_pages.py fails with 'no cubanc_lcf PDF listed'. Worked around by fetching the PDF inside an authenticated Chrome tab (fetch + blob + <a download>) and cutting pages locally with pypdf.

name.evidence: Red case label, image 1: 'CASE NO. 30 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / PROVIDENCIA GRANT / DAVID W. ALEXANDER AND FRANCIS MELLUS CLAIMANT'. Printed transcript title page, stamped PAGE 1 (image 5): 'FOR THE PLACE NAMED "Providencia"'. Departmental Assembly approval calls it 'the tract La Providencia' (stamped PAGE 38, image 48).

year.evidence: Spanish concession decree in the expediente, stamped PAGE 12-13 (images 17-18): 'Angeles Marzo 23 de 1843. Vista la peticion con que da principio este espediente ... declaro a D.n Vicente de la Ossa dueno en propiedad del parage que se halla situado entre el Rancho de los Senores Verdugos ... en estencion de un Sitio de ganado mayor ... El E.S. Gobernador y Comand.te General asi lo mando decreto, y firmo de que doy fe. Michelt.a'. Confirmed by the Departmental Assembly approval (stamped PAGE 38, image 48): 'the tract La Providencia adjudicated in fee on the twenty third day of March one thousand eight hundred & forty three'.

governor.evidence: The concession decree of 23 March 1843 is signed 'Michelt.a' as 'El E.S. Gobernador y Comand.te General' (stamped PAGE 13, image 18); the preceding marginal concession 'Los Angeles Marzo 1.o de 1843, Concedido con las condiciones q.e espresa la prefectura' is likewise signed 'Michelto.a' (stamped PAGE 12, image 17). Board opinion, stamped PAGE 43 (image 54): 'originally granted to one Vicente de la Osa by Governor Manuel Micheltorena on the 23d day of March AD 1843'.

grantee.evidence: Concession decree, stamped PAGE 13 (image 18): 'declaro a D.n Vicente de la Ossa dueno en propiedad del parage'. Departmental Assembly approval, stamped PAGE 38 (image 48): 'We approve the grant made in favor of Don Vicente de la Ossa of the tract La Providencia'. District Court opinion, stamped PAGE 77 (image 89): 'a grant from Governor Michel Torena on the 23rd of March 1843 to one Vicente De la Osa'. The register correctly records the MEXICAN GRANTEE, not the U.S. claimants (David W. land_case.evidence: Red label image 1 'CASE NO. 30 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; flyleaf image 2 'LAND CASE 30 SD PAGES 78'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_sd030.pdf; District Court wrapper 'No 30 Docket' (image 57). Commission docket was No. 338 (transcript title, stamped PAGE 1, image 5; secretary's certificate stamped PAGE 45, image 56), matching Hoffman commission_no 338 / court_no 30.

outcome.evidence: Commission Decree, stamped PAGE 44 (image 55): 'it is adjudged by the Commission that the claim of the said petitioners is valid & it is therefore decreed that the same be confirmed ... known by the name of Providencia ... containing in all one Square League', signed Alpheus Felch, Thompson Campbell, R. Aug. Thompson, filed 18 Oct 1853. On the United States' appeal the District Court also confirmed: opinion at stamped PAGES 77-78 (images 89-90) ends 'A decree will therefore be entered confirming the grant with a reservation of the rights of the Indian Jose Miguel'. Attorney General to the U.S. Attorney, 10 Sept 1856, stamped PAGE 73 (image 85): 'confirmed to the claimants by the Commissioners, Case no. three hundred and thirty-eight (338), and also confirmed on appeal by the District Court, appeal in the Supreme Court will not be prosecuted by the United States', endorsed 'Filed 24th February 1857' (stamped PAGE 74, image 86). Register 'Confirmed' verified at both levels and the Supreme Court appeal abandoned.

notes: Clean record; this is the counter-example to the dominant error class - the claimants (Alexander and Mellus, also the register's patent_to) are all over the file, but the register's grantee field correctly holds the Mexican grantee Vicente de la Osa. Spelling: the Spanish decree and the Departmental Assembly approval both write 'de la Ossa'; the Board opinion, the 1849 deed and the District Court opinion write 'de la Osa'. Register's 'de la Osa' matches the file's own English usage, so no correction. Two 1843 decree dates exist in the expediente and both are 1843: a preliminary concession 'Marzo 1.o de 1843' (stamped PAGE 12) and the definitive decree 'Marzo 23 de 1843' (stamped PAGES 12-13); the grant instrument date is 23 March 1843. Departmental Assembly approval was given at Los Angeles 20 March 1846 by Pio Pico (stamped PAGE 38, image 48) - the claimants' petition says 18 March 1846, which is the date of the Assembly SESSION named in the approval itself. Grant quantity is ONE sitio / one square league, consistent with the register's 4,064.33 patent acres. No patent copy in the file; patent fields left null. name.evidence: Red case label, image 1: 'CASE NO. 118 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / PUNTA DE LA CONCEPCION GRANT / ANASTASIO CARRILLO CLAIMANT'. Printed transcript title, stamped PAGE 1 (image 5): 'FOR THE PLACE NAMED "Punta de la Concepcion"'. The Spanish grant itself calls it 'el terreno conocido con el nombre de la Punta de la Concepcion' (stamped PAGE 7, image 13).

year.evidence: Grant (Document 'A', annexed to the deposition of Pablo de la Guerra), stamped PAGE 8 (image 14): 'Dado en la ex-Mision de S.ta Barbara a 10 de Mayo de 1837. Juan B. Alvarado / Victor Prudon, S.rio into.' Departmental Deputation approval on the same leaf: 'S.ta Barb.a Mayo 18 de 1837. En sesion de este dia aprobo la Exma Diputacion erigida en congreso constituyente el dictamen de la comision ... se concede al C.o Anastacio Carrillo el parage nombrado punta de la concepcion', signed Sta Barbara 14 de Mayo de 1837, Jose R. Estrada (stamped PAGE 9, image 15). The 1839 juridical-possession petition recites the same: 'se le concedio por dho Gobierno con fha 10 de Mayo de 1837, y se aprobo p.r la Exma Diputacion en 18 del mismo mes y ano' (stamped PAGE 10, image 16).

governor.evidence: Grant opening, stamped PAGE 7 (image 13): 'El Ciudadano Juan Bautista Alvarado Gobernador del Estado y Presidente de la Excelentisima Diputacion del mismo. Por cuanto el Ciudadano Anastacio Carrillo ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia el terreno conocido con el nombre de la Punta de la Concepcion'; signed 'Juan B. Alvarado' at stamped PAGE 8 (image 14). Note the title used is 'Gobernador del Estado' (the 1836-38 free-state government), not 'del Departamento'.

grantee.evidence: Grant, stamped PAGE 7 (image 13): 'el Ciudadano Anastacio Carrillo ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia'. Deputation approval, stamped PAGE 8 (image 14): 'se concede al C.o Anastacio Carrillo el parage nombrado punta de la concepcion'. Juridical possession 1839 to 'D.n Anastacio Carrillo' (stamped PAGES 11-12, images 17-18). Register's 'A. Carrillo' is the initialised form (same as Hoffman); the decree spells it 'Anastacio Carrillo'. Same man as the claimant, so no claimant/grantee substitution.

land_case.evidence: Red label image 1 'CASE NO. 118 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; flyleaf image 2 'LAND CASE 118 SD 82 pgs.'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_sd118.pdf; District Court caption 'Docket No. 118' (stamped PAGE 77, image 86). Commission docket was No. 327 (transcript title, stamped PAGE 1, image 5; 'docketed with No. 327', stamped PAGE 2, image 7), matching Hoffman commission_no 327 / court_no 118.

outcome.evidence: TRAP CASE - the Commission REJECTED this claim and the District Court reversed. Docket entry, stamped PAGE 3 (image 9): 'San Francisco Feb. 14, 1854. In the same case Commissioner Thompson Campbell delivered the opinion of the majority of the Board REJECTING the Claim (vide page 21 of this Transcript). In the same case Commissioner R. Aug. Thompson delivered his dissenting opinion (vide page 24 of this Transcript).' On the claimant's appeal the District Court gave judgment for him: order granting the United States an appeal 'from the judgment of this Court AGAINST the United States in the above entitled cause, rendered on or about the 20th day of October A.D. 1855' (stamped PAGE 73, image 82). Attorney General, 16 Sept 1856, stamped PAGE 75 (image 84): '... and also confirmed on appeal by the District Court, appeal in the Supreme Court will not be prosecuted by the United States'. Stipulation vacating the Supreme Court appeal order and making the District Court decree final, filed 5 Feb 1857 (stamped PAGES 77-78, images 86-87). Surveyor General's certificate, stamped PAGE 79 (image 88): 'the Rancho "Punta de Concepcion" confirmed to Anastacio Carrillo has been surveyed by this office ... approved by the U.S. Surveyor General on the 4th day of January 1861', certified copy 28 May 1863, filed 1 June 1863. Final disposition is confirmation, so the register's 'Confirmed' is correct - but only because of the District Court reversal.

notes: THIS IS THE 'Confirmed-only-because-the-District-Court-reversed' CASE the method warns about, and the register's bare 'Confirmed' hides it: the Land Commission majority REJECTED the claim on 14 Feb 1854 (Campbell, with Thompson dissenting); confirmation came from the U.S. District Court, Southern District, judgment rendered on or about 20 Oct 1855, made final by stipulation filed 5 Feb 1857. Single volume, nothing unread that bears on the outcome; the Board's rejection opinion sits at transcript pages 21-23 and Thompson's dissent at 24-33 (PDF images approx. 27-39), which I did not need to read because the docket entry at stamped PAGE 3 states the disposition in terms. WARNING FOR THE CENSUS: the Attorney General's 16 Sept 1856 letter at stamped PAGE 75 is a BOILERPLATE FORM and is factually wrong on this file - it says the claim was 'confirmed to the claimant by the Commissioners, case no. 327', which the Commission never did. An agent grading outcome from that letter alone would record a Commission confirmation that did not happen. The identical form letter appears in SD 030 at its stamped PAGE 73, where it happens to be accurate. Register's patent date of 30 July 1863 is consistent with the file's last document (Surveyor General's certified survey copy, 28 May 1863, filed 1 June 1863) but no patent copy is in the file, so patent fields are left null.

name.evidence: Red case label, image 1: 'CASE NO. 188 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / PUNTA DE LA LAGUNA GRANT / LUIS ARRELLANES ET AL CLAIMANT'. Transcript title, stamped PAGE 1 (image 5): 'FOR THE PLACE NAMED "Punta de la Laguna"'. Expediente cover, stamped PAGE 8 (image 13): 'Espediente promovido por los ciudadanos Luis Are[lla]nes y Emigdio Miguel Ortega en solicitud del parage llamado PUNTA de la LAGUNA. No. 410'.

year.evidence: Titulo, closing clause at stamped PAGE 13 (image 18): 'Dado en Monterey a Veinte y seis de Diciembre de mil ochocientos cuarenta y cuatro. Manuel Michel[torena] / Manuel Jimeno S.rio. Queda tomada razon de esta concesion en el Libro respectivo a fojas 18. Jimeno.' Concession decree, stamped PAGE 10 (image 15): 'Monterey D.bre 26 de 1844. Espidase: Michelt.a / Monterey 26 de D.bre de 1844. Vista la peticion con que da principio este espediente los informes respectivos ... declaro a D.n Emidio Ortega dueno del terreno que solicita.' District Court opinion, stamped PAGE 72 (image 81): 'a grant from Governor Michel Toreno to the present claimants, bearing date 26 December A.D. 1844'.

governor.evidence: Titulo opening, stamped PAGE 12 (image 17): 'El C. Manuel Michelt.a Gral de Brigada del ejercito Mejicano Ayudante General de la Plana Mayor del mismo Gobernador Comand.te Gral y Inspector del Departam.to de las Californias'; signed 'Manuel Michel[torena]' with 'Manuel Jimeno S.rio' at stamped PAGE 13 (image 18). Also 'Espidase: Michelt.a' on the concession decree, stamped PAGE 10 (image 15), and the District Court opinion at stamped PAGE 72 (image 81).

grantee.evidence: Titulo, stamped PAGE 12 (image 17): 'Por cuanto los ciudadanos Luis Are[lla]nes y Emigdio Ortega han pretendido para sus beneficios personales y el de sus familias el parage conocido con el nombre de Punta de la Laguna, colindante con el Rancho de D.n Guillermo Dana, con el de D.n Juan Wilson ... he venido en concederles el terreno mencionado'. Expediente cover names both, stamped PAGE 8 (image 13). District Court caption and opinion: 'The United States, appellants, vs. Luis Arellanes & Emmidio M. Ortega, appellees ... a grant from Governor Michel Toreno TO THE PRESENT CLAIMANTS' (stamped PAGE 72, image 81). Grantees here are also the claimants, so no substitution risk.

land_case.evidence: Red label image 1 'CASE NO. 188 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; flyleaf image 2 'LAND CASE 188 SD pgs. 73'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_sd188.pdf; District Court caption 'Docket No. 188' (stamped PAGE 64, image 73). Commission docket was No. 121 (transcript title, stamped PAGE 1, image 5; 'docketed with No. 121', stamped PAGE 2, image 7), matching Hoffman commission_no 121 / court_no 188. The Mexican expediente carried its own number, No. 410 (stamped PAGE 8, image 13).

outcome.evidence: Commission: docket entry, stamped PAGE 3 (image 8): 'San Francisco May 2d 1854. In the same case Commissioner Thompson Campbell delivered the Opinion of the Board CONFIRMING the Claim (vide page 37 of this Transcript).' District Court opinion, stamped PAGES 72-73 (images 81-82): 'The genuineness and authenticity of the grant is fully proven, the act of judicial possession is also on file and the parol evidence shows a substantial compliance with all the conditions of the grant ... under the rule laid down by the Supreme Court the Claimant is entitled to a confirmation, and a decree will be entered accordingly.' District Court order, December Term 1856, stamped PAGES 64-65 (images 73-74): the Attorney General having given notice that the Supreme Court appeal will not be prosecuted, 'the order granting an appeal to the Supreme Court heretofore made in this cause be and the same is hereby vacated, and that the Claimants have leave to proceed under the decree of this Court heretofore rendered in this cause as under a final decree', signed Isaac S. K. Ogier, U.S. Dist. Judge, endorsed 'Filed Feb 5th 1857'. Register 'Confirmed' verified at both levels and made final.

notes: Clean record on all six fields. ONE INTERNAL DISCREPANCY WORTH FLAGGING for anyone using this file: the concession decree at stamped PAGE 10 (image 15) declares only ONE owner - 'declaro a D.n Emidio Ortega dueno del terreno que solicita' (singular 'dueno', Arellanes not named) - while the titulo issued the same day, 26 Dec 1844, at stamped PAGES 12-13 (images 17-18) grants to BOTH 'los ciudadanos Luis Are[lla]nes y Emigdio Ortega', and the District Court read it as a grant 'to the present claimants' plural. The titulo is the operative instrument, so the register's two-grantee reading is right; an agent grading only from the marginal decree would wrongly drop Arellanes. Background in the expediente: the pair first bought out the Purisima Indians' claim (padre Juan Moreno's contract of 25 Sept 1843 for 100 head of cattle and 12 horses, stamped PAGE 11, image 16) before the grant issued. Grant quantity six sitios de ganado mayor (stamped PAGE 12, image 17), consistent with the register's 26,648.42 patent acres. No patent copy in the file; patent fields left null. Judicial possession and later District Court testimony (Juan Jose Lusaraga, stamped PAGES 66-70, images 75-79) are witness evidence and were not used for grading.

name.evidence: Red case label, image 1: 'CASE NO. 372 / NORTHERN DISTRICT / PUNTA de QUINTIN GRANT / B. R. BUCKELEW CLAIMANT'. Transcript title, stamped PAGE 1 (image 5): 'FOR THE PLACE NAMED "Punta de Quintin"'. The grant itself names it 'la Punta de Quintin, Corte de Madera y la Laguna' (Spanish titulo, stamped PAGE 34, image 41).

year.evidence: Spanish titulo (Exhibit No. 1 to David Spence's deposition), closing clause at stamped PAGE 35 (image 42): 'Dado en Monterrey a veinte y cuatro de Septiembre de mil ocho cientos Cuarenta. Juan B. Alvarado. Manuel Jimeno Srio. Queda tomada razon de este titulo en el libro de asientos sobre adjudicaciones de terrenos validos a fojas 3.a Jimeno.' Sworn translation 'B' of title and juridical possession, stamped PAGE 41 (image 48): 'Given in Monterey on the twenty fourth of September, One thousand eight hundred & forty. (Signed) Juan B. Alvarado. (Signed) Manuel Jimeno, secretary.'

governor.evidence: Titulo opening, stamped PAGE 34 (image 41): 'Juan B. Alvarado, Gobernador Constitucional del Departamento de las Californias. Por cuanto Don Juan Cooper ha pretendido para su veneficio personal y el de su familia el parage conocido con el nombre de la Punta de Quintin, Corte de Madera y la Laguna con la exclusion de la Canada de San Anselmo mientras de las indios la estan ocupando'. Translation at stamped PAGE 40 (image 47): 'Juan B. Alvarado, Constitutional Governor of the Department of the Californias'. Board opinion, stamped PAGE 54 (image 61): 'founded on a grant made by Governor Juan B. Alvarado'.

grantee.evidence: Titulo, stamped PAGE 34 (image 41): 'Por cuanto Don Juan Cooper ha pretendido para su veneficio personal y el de su familia'; translation stamped PAGE 40 (image 47): 'Whereas don Juan Cooper has for his own personal benefit and that of his family petitioned for the place known by the name of Punta de Quintin'. land_case.evidence: Red label image 1 'CASE NO. 372 / NORTHERN DISTRICT'; flyleaf image 2 'LAND CASE 372 ND 65 pages'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_nd372.pdf; District Court wrapper 'U.S. District Court, Northern District of California, No. 372' (image 65) and decree caption 'D.C. 372; L.C. 740' (stamped PAGE 63, image 70). Commission docket was No. 740 (transcript title, stamped PAGE 1, image 5; secretary's certificate, stamped PAGE 57, image 64), matching Hoffman commission_no 740 / court_no 372.

outcome.evidence: Commission: opinion of Comr. R. Aug. Thompson, stamped PAGE 54 (image 61), ending 'The evidence shows a full compliance with the conditions of the grant, and the boundaries are defined with sufficient certainty ... a decree of confirmation will be entered. Confirmed. Filed in Office July 10, 1855.' Decree of Confirmation, stamped PAGE 55 (image 62): 'it is adjudged by the Commission that the claim of the Petitioner is valid and it is therefore decreed that the same be confirmed. The land of which confirmation is made is known by the name of "Punta de Quintin" situated in the County of Marin, containing two square leagues a little more or less', signed R. Aug. Thompson and S. B. Farwell, filed 10 July 1855. District Court, Stated Term March 30, 1857, stamped PAGES 60-61 (images 67-68): 'the Court is of opinion that there is no error in the decision of the said board, and that the same should be, and the same hereby is in all things affirmed ... the claim of the said appellee is a good and valid claim, and the same is hereby confirmed to him to the extent and quantity of two square leagues, a little more or less', signed Ogden Hoffman, U.S. Dist. Judge, filed 30 March 1857. Register 'Confirmed' verified at both levels. SEE NOTES: the file then ends with a Supreme Court appeal GRANTED and no disposition of it.

notes: All six register fields verified against the grant instrument itself, which IS in this file in both languages (Spanish titulo at stamped PAGES 34-35, images 41-42; sworn translation 'B' at stamped PAGES 40-41, images 47-48), filed as Exhibit No. 1 to David Spence's deposition rather than transcribed in the body of the transcript - an agent reading only the transcript's first 30 images would find nothing but the claimant's petition and depositions and might wrongly grade UV or grade off the petition. ⚠ OUTCOME CAVEAT: this file does NOT close. Its last substantive document is a District Court order of 1 April 1857, stamped PAGE 63 (image 70), signed by Ogden Hoffman: 'It is Ordered by the Court that an appeal in behalf of the United States from the final decision of this Court, rendered at the present term, be, and the same is hereby granted; and that a certified transcript of the pleadings, evidence, depositions and proceedings in the said cause be sent to the Supreme Court without delay', endorsed 'Filed April 1st 1857'. There is no dismissal, stipulation or Supreme Court mandate in the volume, so the appeal's fate is NOT shown here. I still graded outcome OK because the register's claim (confirmation) is what both the Commission and the District Court decreed, Hoffman's 1862 table also records 'confirmed', and a patent followed in 1866; but a re-reader wanting the appeal's disposition must look outside this file. ⚠ DATE SLIP INSIDE THE FILE: the Board's own opinion at stamped PAGE 54 says the grant was made 'on the 4th day of September 1840', while the titulo and its sworn translation both say the TWENTY-FOURTH of September 1840, as does the claimant's petition (stamped PAGE 5, image 11). Year unaffected. Grant quantity two square leagues, consistent with the register's 8,877.44 patent acres. The grant expressly EXCLUDED the Canada de San Anselmo 'mientras de las indios la estan ocupando' / 'while the Indians continue to occupy it' (stamped PAGES 34 and 40); Timothy Murphy's certificate of 8 Oct 1846 that the canada had been unoccupied for two years is bound into the title papers (stamped PAGES 35 and 41). No patent copy in the file; patent fields left null.

name.evidence: Red case label, image 1: 'CASE NO. 236 / NORTHERN DISTRICT / PUNTA DE LOS REYES GRANT / ANDREW RANDALL CLAIMANT'. Transcript title, stamped PAGE 1 (image 5): 'FOR THE PLACE NAMED "Punta de los Reyes"'. The grant itself calls it 'el parage conocido con el Nombre de punta de Reyes' (titulo, stamped PAGE 43, image 49). The register's parenthetical '(Sobrante)' was NOT seen in any page I read; it comes from the Bancroft catalogue title ('Punta de los Reyes (also called Sobrante)'), which is consistent with the grant being of the surplus left after Snook's and Berry's and Garcia's tracts, but I did not verify the word in the file.

year.evidence: Concession decree in the expediente, stamped PAGE 41 (image 47): 'Monterey 30 de Noviembre de 1843. Vista la peticion con que da principio este espediente los informes que preceden ... de conformidad con las leyes y reglamento de la Materia, declaro a D.n Ant.o M.a Osio dueno en propiedad del parage nombrado punta de Reyes ... en estencion de once sitios de ganado mayor sin comprender los dos sitios que se le habian concedido a D.n Jose Shoke [Snook]. Librese el correspondiente despacho ... Micheltorena'. Titulo (Exhibit No. 1 to the deposition of David Spence, 1 Nov 1853), closing clause at stamped PAGE 44 (image 50): 'Dado en Monterey a treinta de Noviembre de mil ocho cientos cuarenta y tres. Man.l Michelt.a / Man.l Jimeno S.rio.' Board opinion, stamped PAGE 89 (image 99): 'a grant of the land claimed, made by Governor Manuel Micheltorena to Antonio Maria Osio under date of November 30, 1843'.

governor.evidence: Titulo opening, stamped PAGE 43 (image 49): 'Manuel Micheltorena General de Brigada del Ejercito Mejicano Ayudante General de la plana mayor del mismo Gobernador Comandante General e Inspector del Departamento de las Californias'; signed 'Man.l Michelt.a' at stamped PAGE 44 (image 50). Earlier in the same expediente: Micheltorena's order for a report, 'Monterey Oct.e 26 de 1843 ... Michelt.a' (stamped PAGE 39, image 45) and his decree of 28 Oct 1843 'Como opina el S.r Ofic.l del Despacho a favor y en justicia de S. Osio y estando valdio el terreno espidasele el titulo ... Micheltorena' (stamped PAGES 40-41, images 46-47).

grantee.evidence: Concession decree, stamped PAGE 41 (image 47): 'declaro a D.n Ant.o M.a Osio dueno en propiedad del parage nombrado punta de Reyes'. Titulo, stamped PAGE 43 (image 49): 'Por cuanto D. Antonio Maria Osio ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia el parage conocido con el Nombre de punta de Reyes, colindante con D.n Jaume Ricardo Berri y D.n Rafael Garcia'. Commission decree, stamped PAGE 91 (image 101): 'the same granted to and formerly occupied by Antonio Maria Osio'. The register correctly records the MEXICAN GRANTEE, not the U.S. claimant Andrew Randall, who bought from Osio and wife by deed of 8 Jan 1852 (Board opinion, stamped PAGE 89, image 99).

notes: Clean record on all six fields, and another counter-example to the dominant error class: the claimant Andrew Randall is the register's patent_to, while the grantee field correctly holds Antonio Maria Osio. WATCH THE TWO-STAGE GRANT: the claimant's own derraignment at stamped PAGES 5-6 (images 11-12) lists TWO concessions, (B) 'A Marginal Decree by Juan B. Alvarado then the Governor of California granting the land asked for with the understanding that the Grantee should take the customary proceedings, dated January 4, 1842' and (G) 'An Absolute Grant by Micheltorena ... dated Novr. 30, 1843'. The Alvarado marginal decree is physically in the file at stamped PAGE 38 (image 44) and reads 'Monterey En.o 21 de 1842. De conformidad con lo que pide el interesado en esta representacion se le concede el terreno mencionado en concepto de que para obtener el titulo q.e corresponde presentara de nuevo por mamado el diseno respectivo y corrido los tramites del estilo. Alvarado' - i.e. an 1842 PROVISIONAL concession requiring the grantee to come back for a title, on a petition of 3 Oct 1840. The register's 1843/Micheltorena is the definitive grant and is right; an agent grading off the 1842 marginal decree would wrongly report 1842/Alvarado. (Note also that the manuscript date of that marginal decree looks like 'Enero 21' where the claimant's petition and Bowman both say January 4; I could not resolve the numeral confidently and it does not affect any graded field.) The 1841-44 boundary war with Jaime Ricardo Berry and Rafael Garcia runs through the whole expediente and was settled by a decree of the Superior Tribunal of Justice of the Department, 29 Feb 1844 (fiscal's opinion 28 Feb 1844 at stamped PAGES 45-47, images 51-53). PATENT: no patent copy is in the file, so patent fields are left null, BUT the file recites one - Circuit Judge M. Hall McAllister's order of 2 July 1860 (stamped PAGE 111, image 125) says 'it further appearing that the patent upon said survey and plat has been duly issued by the proper Department at Washington, received by the said Surveyor General for Cala, and by him transferred to the legal representatives of the said Claimant', which corroborates the register's patent date of 4 June 1860. Note for Phase C: by then Randall's interest had passed by conveyance to Solomon Heydenfeldt, O. L. Shafter, J. McM. Shafter and T. W. Park, who were substituted into the record by order filed 3 June 1859 (stamped PAGE 103, image 121), so 'patent_to: Andrew Randall' is the name on the patent, not the beneficial owner. Quantity: the grant maximum is eleven sitios, but the Board noted the surveyed quantity was 'found to be less than ten square leagues' and therefore that 'there can be therefore no surplus to be reserved to the Nation' (stamped PAGES 90-91, images 100-101); the register's patent acreage of 48,189.34 acres is about 10.8 leagues.
